posts.title: Binance resumes withdrawals following $6.3 billion breach | TechCrunch
posts.author: Anthony Ha
posts.summary: Binance has begun phased withdrawals after a $6.3 billion hack that froze deposits and withdrawals. The exchange says it has recovered 95 % of the stolen crypto and is still sourcing the remaining assets, which are less liquid. The FBI has identified a North Korean group, TraderTraitor, as the culprit, and Binance processed $4.6 billion in withdrawals and $1 billion in deposits, leaving a net outflow of $3.6 billion. Binance will continue to strengthen security, complete the recovery, and release a detailed incident report once the investigation finishes.
key_points: Binance resumes withdrawals in phases after a $6.3 billion hack
95 % of stolen assets recovered, remaining assets still being sourced
FBI links hack to North Korean group TraderTraitor
Net outflow of $3.6 billion during initial withdrawal period

posts.title: Exclusive: Here’s what 'renoa' — the first new fiber in 25 years — feels like | TechCrunch
posts.author: Tim De Chant
posts.summary: Everbloom’s new fiber, renoa, has become the first new fiber classification in 25 years after approval by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, offering a washable and affordable alternative to expensive cashmere. Made from waste protein scraps such as cashmere, wool, down, and feather lint, the material is blended with a biodegradable biopolymer and extruded to mimic natural fibers. The startup, which has been developing the fiber for three years and built its own AI material‑science model, plans to launch its first consumer product—a cashmere‑renoa blend sweater—in the second quarter of 2027. Renoa’s 80/20 blend delivers a feel close to real cashmere while resisting pilling, shrinking, and requiring minimal finishing, positioning it as a sustainable, high‑performance textile for mainstream apparel.
key_points: Renoa is the first new fiber classification in 25 years, approved by the FTC.
It is produced from waste protein scraps and is washable, affordable, and biodegradable.
Everbloom is scaling up production and expects its first consumer product to hit the market in Q2 2027.
An 80/20 cashmere‑renoa blend mimics real cashmere’s softness and durability without pilling or shrinking.

posts.title: I took two iPhones on vacation — the Duo won me over | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Sarah Perez tested Apple’s new iPhone Duo on a five‑day vacation, initially frustrated by its small screen, unoptimized apps, and the return to Touch ID, but ultimately grew to appreciate its durability and pocket‑friendly design. The $2,000 device proved surprisingly robust, surviving multiple drops on hard surfaces without damage, and its compact, squat shape fit comfortably in both front and back pockets. While the Duo’s lack of Face ID and occasional app freezes—particularly in Google Search’s AI mode—remained notable drawbacks, Perez found that most major apps were quickly updated for the new form factor and that her Apple Watch provided a convenient alternative for authentication. The experience highlighted the psychological switching cost of moving from a high‑end iPhone 17 Pro Max to an experimental device, yet Perez concluded that the Duo’s strengths ultimately won her over.
key_points: The iPhone Duo’s compact, squat design fits comfortably in pockets and survived multiple drops without damage.
Users may face frustrations with small screen real estate, unoptimized apps, and the return to Touch ID, especially during payments.
Major apps quickly updated for Duo, but early reviews noted black bars on non‑optimized apps and occasional freezes in Google Search’s AI mode.

posts.title: Last-minute Halloween costumes for tech nerds | TechCrunch
posts.author: Amanda Silberling
posts.summary: TechCrunch’s latest article offers a playful guide to last‑minute Halloween costumes for tech enthusiasts. The suggestions span AI concepts such as recursive self‑improvement, cute AI agent avatars, and even a mock “Claude token limit” notification. It also pokes fun at real‑world tech personalities, from Mark Zuckerberg’s signature black tees to biohacker Bryan Johnson’s controversial GLP‑Bryan claim. The piece blends humor with subtle reminders about privacy, AI safety, and the cultural impact of technology on everyday life.
key_points: TechCrunch provides a list of tech‑themed Halloween costumes, including AI concepts and real‑world tech figures.
The ideas range from recursive self‑improvement to AI assistants with cute avatars and mock usage‑limit alerts.
The article humorously references personalities like Mark Zuckerberg and biohacker Bryan Johnson.
It also highlights privacy concerns and AI safety in a light‑hearted context.

posts.title: Pixel 11 Pro Fold: Sturdy rectangle in a wide, wide world | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: Google has launched the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, a foldable that builds on last year’s design with a lighter chassis, a brighter 3,600‑nit display, and a 19‑gram weight reduction. The phone boasts a 48‑megapixel main sensor, 30× Super‑Res Zoom, and a three‑fold increase in durability thanks to a glass‑ceramic cover and glass‑fiber composite back. Priced at $1,899, it sits just below the iPhone Duo and matches the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, but faces stiff competition from emerging wide‑foldables in Europe. While the device offers solid cameras and useful software features like Magic Capture, its visible crease and one‑handed hinge design may deter first‑time foldable buyers.
key_points: Google’s Pixel 11 Pro Fold is lighter, brighter, and three times more durable than its predecessor, featuring a 3,600‑nit display and a 48‑MP main sensor with 30× Super‑Res Zoom
The phone’s cameras are competent but still lag behind the slab Pixel 11 Pro XL, and the device supports useful software such as Magic Capture and Looks
At $1,899 it competes with the iPhone Duo and Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, yet the foldable market is crowded with new wide‑format models from Xiaomi and Honor
The hinge design prevents one‑handed unfolding, and the visible crease remains a drawback compared to rivals that have reduced crease visibility

posts.title: Apple CEO says the company doesn’t ‘want to ship AI for AI’s sake’ | TechCrunch
posts.author: Anthony Ha
posts.summary: Apple CEO John Ternus told Wired that Apple is not rushing to ship AI for AI’s sake but will integrate it into products in a way that feels natural to users. He acknowledged that Apple has been seen as lagging behind, especially after a delayed, more powerful Siri launch this summer, yet he expressed confidence in the company’s current AI direction. Ternus emphasized that the goal is to build products people love, rather than to showcase AI for its own sake. He also noted that while AI could reduce the need for traditional apps, the act of creating products remains a deeply human endeavor.
key_points: Apple’s new CEO says AI will be integrated thoughtfully, not for hype
Apple has been behind on AI but is improving with a new Siri release
The focus is on building beloved products, not just AI features
Human creativity remains central even as AI changes app development

posts.title: How Founder Summit helps you make more useful connections to scale | TechCrunch
posts.author: TechCrunch Events
posts.summary: TechCrunch’s Founder Summit will take place on November 4 at Boston’s SoWa Power Station and is presented by Fidelity Private Shares. The event focuses on intentional networking, offering a Braindate-powered lounge where founders and VCs can schedule one‑on‑one and small‑group conversations around specific topics. Attendees can also participate in roundtables, breakout sessions, an Expo Hall, and a closing reception, with side events running throughout Boston that week. A buy‑one‑get‑one‑free ticket promotion is available, allowing participants to bring a co‑founder or partner at no extra cost while saving up to $100 on the pass.

Sessions on product‑market fit, fundraising, and local building are followed by dedicated conversation opportunities.
A buy‑one‑get‑one‑free pass promotion and up to $100 savings are offered before the event starts.

posts.title: Salesforce’s M&A spree continues with a reported $375M deal for defense tech startup Rune | TechCrunch
posts.author: Marina Temkin
posts.summary: Salesforce has agreed to acquire defense‑tech startup Rune Technologies for $375 million in cash and stock. The deal expands Salesforce’s Missionforce unit, which already grew 80% YoY after securing a $5.6 billion, 10‑year contract with the U.S. Army, and will now integrate Rune’s AI‑driven logistics platform to support battlefield operations. Rune, founded in 2024, has raised $30 million from investors such as Andreessen Horowitz and IQT, and was last valued at $127 million. This acquisition is part of Salesforce’s broader 2024 acquisition spree that also includes Fin, Qualified, and Listen Labs.
key_points: Salesforce is buying Rune Technologies for $375 million to boost its Missionforce defense‑tech unit.
Rune’s AI logistics platform will help the U.S. military predict supply needs and manage field operations.
The acquisition follows Salesforce’s 2024 spree that added Fin, Qualified, and Listen Labs to its portfolio.

posts.title: OpenAI reportedly lowers funding target for new round | TechCrunch
posts.author: Anthony Ha
posts.summary: OpenAI has cut its latest funding round target from the previously reported $30 billion to $20 billion, with the first close expected to be even lower. The round, led by investors from the United Arab Emirates, has already raised $11 billion, but the company has received a tepid response from some large investors amid a broader market wariness of heavy AI infrastructure spending. The timing of the fundraising coincides with a sell‑off in tech stocks and the potential challenges facing Anthropic’s planned IPO, both of which may be dampening investor enthusiasm. If a subsequent retail offering for wealthy individuals is completed, the total funding could reach the $20 billion target, but the current trajectory suggests a more modest outcome.
key_points: OpenAI lowered its funding target from $30B to $20B
The round has already raised $11B and is led by UAE investors
Investor enthusiasm has been tepid amid AI infrastructure spending concerns
A retail offering could bring the total to $20B if completed

posts.title: From restaurant guides to payments, here’s how TikTok is building a super app | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aisha Malik
posts.summary: TikTok is expanding beyond social media by adding a restaurant guide called "Must Eat" that aggregates over 40 million posts to recommend eateries, and by developing a direct‑message money transfer feature that would use its TikTok Pay service. The company also launched TikTok GO, a booking hub for hotels and attractions, and has applied for fintech licenses in Brazil to offer lending and payment services. These moves are part of TikTok’s strategy to become a super app that handles shopping, dining, travel, and financial transactions in one place, directly competing with platforms like WeChat, Yelp, Google Maps, and Amazon. The expansion follows the success of TikTok Shop, which grew U.S. sales by 407% in 2024 and is now a significant player in social commerce.
key_points: TikTok introduces "Must Eat" restaurant guide to compete with Yelp and Google Maps
The platform is developing a direct‑message money transfer feature using TikTok Pay
TikTok GO lets users book hotels and attractions within the app, moving into travel commerce
These initiatives signal TikTok’s push toward a super‑app model that blends social media, e‑commerce, and fintech

posts.title: Pile-ins, payouts, and pacing pressure: the investors behind the VCs open up | TechCrunch
posts.author: Connie Loizos
posts.summary: Limited partners are currently pouring capital into a handful of AI companies, notably OpenAI and Anthropic, creating unprecedented concentration in venture portfolios. The rapid rise in valuations has prompted LPs to accelerate fund cycles, with some returning capital in as little as 12 to 18 months, a pace that raises concerns about risk and distribution timing. Despite the speed, many LPs view the consolidation as a natural evolution of the power‑law nature of venture investing, though they remain wary of potential downturns. The conversation with LGT Capital Partners and TrueBridge highlights both excitement for the upside and caution about the sustainability of such aggressive deployment strategies.
key_points: LPs are heavily concentrating investments in OpenAI and Anthropic, breaking traditional diversification norms.
Fund cycles are shortening to 12‑18 months, increasing deployment speed and raising distribution concerns.
Venture managers are bumping up fund sizes mid‑cycle to capture large AI rounds, creating a “yellow light” scenario for LPs.
Early‑stage funds still offer diversity, but late‑stage concentration is accelerating.

posts.title: Nvidia weighs playing the cosigner for Nscale’s AI data center in West Virginia | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aditya Mehta
posts.summary: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to act as a co‑signer for billions‑of‑dollar debt financing that will fund Anthropic’s first building at Nscale’s West Virginia AI data‑center campus. The arrangement would give Nvidia a residual‑value guarantee, allowing it to step in if Nscale defaults on construction payments and help secure a buyer or tenant. The move underscores the financial strain on AI cloud providers as investors grow wary of the scale of capital required, and it deepens Nvidia’s ties to Nscale while securing a major customer for its Vera Rubin chips. Anthropic’s $44.6 billion contract for the 460‑MW building and a potential second $45 billion deal highlight the high stakes of the project amid construction setbacks and regulatory hurdles.
key_points: Nvidia is poised to co‑sign debt for Anthropic’s West Virginia data‑center, offering a residual‑value guarantee.
The guarantee would let Nvidia take over if Nscale defaults, helping secure a buyer or tenant for the campus.
Anthropic’s $44.6 billion contract for the first 460‑MW building and a potential $45 billion second deal illustrate the massive scale of the project.
The deal reflects growing investor caution and the need for AI cloud providers to secure financing amid construction and regulatory challenges.

posts.title: Applebee's exposed customers' personal data after leaving database password in app | TechCrunch
posts.author: Zack Whittaker
posts.summary: Applebee’s fixed a security flaw that allowed anyone to access its customer database after a researcher discovered a hardcoded credential in the chain’s Android app. The exposed data included names, email addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers, ZIP codes, veteran status, login counts, account creation dates, and recent IP addresses. Applebee’s and parent Dine Brands said they investigated the issue and found no evidence of unauthorized access, but the exact number of affected customers remains unknown; the rewards program had 8.5 million members last year. The incident underscores the risks of hardcoding credentials and the need for proper vulnerability disclosure channels.
key_points: A hardcoded credential in Applebee’s Android app exposed the customer database.
The data contained personal details and login information such as IP addresses.
Applebee’s and Dine Brands investigated and found no evidence of a breach yet.
The researcher could not alert the company due to lack of reporting mechanisms.

posts.title: Google's first data center satellite is online and writing poetry | TechCrunch
posts.author: Tim Fernholz
posts.summary: Google’s Suncatcher prototype satellite, launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 in early October, is now online and communicating with the ground while carrying four Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) that can generate up to 1 kW of power. The satellite’s first test involved asking Google DeepMind’s Gemma 4 model to compose a haiku about space, demonstrating the ability to run inference workloads in orbit, though only one TPU can be powered on for about 20 minutes at a time due to power constraints. Engineers are now evaluating how the chips perform under thermal stress and space radiation, which can cause bit flips that corrupt data, and the results will inform plans to launch two additional, higher‑power satellites in 2027 with inter‑satellite optical links. The project is part of Google’s broader vision for orbital data centers and is closely tied to SpaceX’s Starship development, with Alphabet holding a significant stake in the launch provider.
key_points: Suncatcher satellite is online, carries four TPUs, and has written a poetry haiku using DeepMind’s Gemma 4.
Only one TPU can be powered on at a time, limiting operation to roughly 20 minutes per cycle due to power constraints.
Ground tests are assessing radiation effects on the TPUs, which could cause bit flips and data corruption in space.
If successful, Google plans to launch two more satellites in 2027 with higher power and optical inter‑satellite links, relying on SpaceX’s Starship rocket.

posts.title: Founder Summit in 6 days in Boston | TechCrunch

posts.summary: TechCrunch’s Founder Summit will take place in Boston on November 4, offering founders, investors, and operators a day of breakout and roundtable sessions focused on real‑world lessons from scaling and growth. The event, presented by Fidelity Private Shares, features speakers such as Toast’s Steve Fredette, Bessemer’s Kent Bennett, and Cogent Security’s Vineet Edupuganti, who will discuss topics from reinvention to team building. Attendees can take advantage of promotional offers, including a buy‑one‑get‑one‑free ticket and up to 30% off group bundles, before the doors open. Speakers include Toast’s Steve Fredette, Bessemer’s Kent Bennett, and Cogent Security’s Vineet Edupuganti, covering scaling, growth, and team building.
Promotional deals offer a free second ticket or up to 30% off group bundles before the event starts.

posts.title: Intel's stock crashes, knocking $12B from government's stake | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: Intel’s shares plunged about 28% on Friday after the company issued a weaker‑than‑expected fourth‑quarter outlook, causing the U.S. government’s 10% stake to lose roughly $12 billion in value. The downgrade came as Intel projected revenue of $15‑$16 billion versus analysts’ $17 billion estimate and warned its gross‑margin would fall to 37% from 43%, while it expected no positive cash flow. Despite the sharp drop, the government still holds a profitable position, with Intel up more than 70% year‑to‑date, and Nvidia’s stake also saw a modest decline. The company cited a PC slowdown driven by high memory prices and AI demand, but noted a 78% jump in data‑center revenue, though capacity expansion is delayed until new fabs become operational in 2028.
key_points: Intel’s stock fell 28% after a weaker Q4 outlook, wiping $12 billion off the government’s stake.
The company warned of lower revenue ($15‑$16 billion) and a margin drop to 37%, with no expected positive cash flow.
PC sales are pressured by AI‑driven memory demand, while data‑center revenue grew 78% but is limited by fab capacity.
The government’s 10% Intel holding remains profitable, up over 70% year‑to‑date, despite the sharp decline.

posts.title: Anthropic expected to receive high 'junk' rating from credit agencies following IPO, FT report says | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lucas Ropek
posts.summary: Anthropic is expected to receive a high "junk" rating from credit agencies after its IPO, according to a Financial Times report. Blackstone, the anchor investor in a $63 billion chip‑financing deal, now predicts a double‑B range rating, a top tier of speculative junk, after previously saying the company would be investment‑grade before 2027. A high junk rating would raise borrowing costs and make it harder for Anthropic to finance its large compute‑spending spree. The filing for the IPO earlier this week has intensified speculation about the impact on the broader AI industry.
key_points: Blackstone now forecasts a double‑B junk rating for Anthropic post‑IPO
The prediction contrasts with earlier investment‑grade expectations
A high junk rating could increase borrowing costs and limit funding
Anthropic’s heavy compute spending has raised investor concerns

posts.title: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom | TechCrunch
posts.author: Rebecca Bellan
posts.summary: Investors are growing uneasy about the massive AI infrastructure spend announced by Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft, which together plan over $740 billion in capital expenditures this year. The news has triggered a sharp sell‑off, with the Nasdaq falling 2.9% and major chip stocks like Nvidia, Broadcom, and Qualcomm dropping 4–11%, while Alphabet’s shares plunged 12% and wiped out $500 billion in market value. Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta are reporting negative free cash flow, raising concerns that the hefty AI outlays may erode the profitability of their core businesses, whereas Microsoft remains the only firm with positive free cash flow. The surge in debt—$326 billion raised in 2026—combined with the looming Anthropic IPO, underscores the financial strain on the sector as demand for AI compute remains high.
key_points: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft plan more than $740 billion in AI‑related capex this year
Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta are reporting negative free cash flow while Microsoft stays positive
The Nasdaq and major chip stocks fell sharply after the announcements, and Alphabet lost $500 billion in market value
$326 billion of debt was raised by the big tech firms in 2026, and Anthropic’s IPO faces potential junk‑rating concerns

posts.title: Ollie, a privacy-focused AI assistant, is shutting down | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lucas Ropek
posts.summary: Ollie, a privacy‑focused AI assistant startup, announced it will shut down on November 6 after a week of announcement. Co‑founder Bill Lennon said the small team built an impressive personal assistant, but competition from larger players like Muse and Instinct made it hard to raise capital and stand out. The app offered a subscription‑based service that integrated email, calendar, appointment booking, meal planning, bill payments, and planned household budgeting, and was one of the first mainstream apps to achieve SOC 2 compliance. Users will receive instructions to export data and receive refunds.
key_points: Ollie will shut down on November 6 after a week of announcement
The startup raised $7.5 million in seed funding led by Khosla Ventures and achieved SOC 2 compliance
Competition from larger AI assistants made it difficult to grow and secure funding
Users will be guided to export data and receive refunds

posts.title: Satlyt takes another step toward turning satellites into space data centers | TechCrunch
posts.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
posts.summary: Satlyt, a 2024 startup founded by former Google and SpaceX engineer Rama Afullo, demonstrated its software’s ability to orchestrate computing tasks across multiple satellites during a NASA‑funded test that ran on a physical computer aboard a spacecraft. The experiment, conducted in partnership with the University of Houston, showed the system could generate task‑allocation plans in orbit while accounting for limited compute, intermittent communication, and user‑defined constraints. Although the software successfully executed and returned results to Earth, the team identified a timing‑reference bug and noted that further validation is needed before deploying the technology on real missions. Satlyt aims to turn spacecraft into virtual data centers that can run AI and other applications onboard, reducing reliance on downlinks and enabling faster, more efficient data delivery from space to Earth.
key_points: Satlyt’s NASA‑funded test proved its software can plan and execute distributed computing tasks on orbiting hardware.
The system allows operators to set permissions, priorities, and limits while autonomously managing task allocation across satellites.
Further work is required to address timing bugs, secure communication, and broader validation before deployment on actual missions.

posts.title: Zest's new AI agent finds restaurants and books reservations over text | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Zest, a restaurant discovery app launched in November 2024, has unveiled an AI‑powered "restaurant concierge" that operates via text messages, allowing users to receive personalized recommendations and book tables directly through services like OpenTable, Resy, and SevenRooms. The concierge pulls data from users’ credit‑card transactions via Plaid to build a taste profile, enabling it to suggest restaurants based on cuisine, location, dietary needs, and even group preferences in group chats. The startup, backed by $1.8 million in pre‑seed funding from Alexis Ohanian’s 776 and Steve Jang’s Kindred Ventures, plans to expand beyond dining to other recommendation domains while monetizing through booking and future ordering revenue streams. The feature was tested in TechCrunch trials, showing reliable suggestions and booking capability, and is now live for users to text at (212) 470‑6067.
key_points: Zest introduces a text‑based AI concierge that recommends restaurants and books tables via OpenTable, Resy, and SevenRooms
It uses Plaid‑imported credit‑card food transactions to build personalized taste profiles
The startup has $1.8 million pre‑seed funding and aims to monetize through bookings and future ordering
The concierge can operate in group chats, voting, and handle dietary or occasion queries

posts.title: Theranos whistleblower Tyler Shultz warns that the AI boom is 'a great opportunity to go deceive people' | TechCrunch
posts.author: Amanda Silberling
posts.summary: Tyler Shultz, the whistleblower who exposed Theranos’ faulty blood‑testing technology, warns that the current AI boom gives unscrupulous founders a new platform to deceive investors and the public. He cites the Theranos scandal—where a $10 billion valuation was built on unreliable devices—as a cautionary tale that investors must not repeat. Shultz argues that AI products are harder to vet, making it easier to disguise a ChatGPT wrapper as a breakthrough. The documentary “You Can See Everything” has reignited public interest in Holmes, but Shultz stresses that the real lesson is about due diligence in the age of AI.
key_points: Shultz warns that the AI boom offers a new avenue for deception similar to Theranos’ fraud
The Theranos scandal highlighted the dangers of insufficient due diligence for high‑valuation startups
Investors in AI face challenges in distinguishing genuine innovation from superficial wrappers
The documentary “You Can See Everything” has sparked renewed debate about Holmes and corporate fraud

posts.title: Andy Jassy says Prime Video is on track to earn 'tens of billions of dollars' | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy announced on the Q2 earnings call that Prime Video is on track to generate tens of billions in revenue and is already profitable. The streaming arm has benefited from Amazon MGM Studios’ box‑office successes, including the $684 million‑grossing "Project Hail Mary" and other hits such as "Verity." Prime Video also drives viewership through popular TV series like "Reacher," "The Boys," and "Carrie," and sports rights to NASCAR, the Masters, UEFA Champions League, and Thursday Night Football. The combination of original content, sports programming, and a growing subscriber base positions Prime Video as a major revenue engine for Amazon’s broader media strategy.
key_points: Prime Video is projected to generate tens of billions in revenue and is already profitable
Amazon MGM Studios has earned over $1.2 billion in global box office sales this year
Prime Video’s sports rights, especially Thursday Night Football, are driving high viewership
Original series such as Reacher and The Boys are key content drivers

posts.title: Where was my invite to the — wait, what? Airbnb had a gala? | TechCrunch
posts.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
posts.summary: Airbnb’s nonprofit hosted its first gala in Los Angeles on October 28, a night that featured Jimmy Kimmel, Charli XCX, and a host of A‑list celebrities. The event announced a new program in which Airbnb will donate 10 cents of every commercial booking revenue to the nonprofit, aiming to raise $500 million over five years to fund free housing for one million nights annually. The initiative also expands support to families displaced by domestic violence, veterans, and medical travelers. While the gala drew media attention and celebrity presence, many online observers were puzzled by the company’s decision to hold a high‑profile fundraising event.
key_points: Airbnb’s nonprofit held its inaugural gala in Los Angeles on October 28.
The gala launched a program that will donate 10 cents per stay to the nonprofit, targeting $500 million over five years.
The funds will provide free housing for one million nights each year and support families facing displacement.
Celebrity attendance and the event’s high‑profile nature sparked confusion among the public.

posts.title: North Korean hackers blamed for stealing record $6.3B in Binance breach | TechCrunch
posts.author: Zack Whittaker
posts.summary: North Korean hackers are blamed for the largest recorded cryptocurrency theft, stealing at least $6.3 billion from Binance in a 20‑minute breach that began with a compromised engineer’s laptop. Binance has frozen roughly half the stolen assets and is working with law‑enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms, and industry partners to trace and recover the funds, while suspending deposits and withdrawals. Security researchers say the attackers, known as TraderTraitor, used a service container to submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions without compromising Binance’s private keys. The incident underscores the vulnerability of crypto exchanges to insider‑device attacks and highlights the ongoing threat posed by state‑backed hacking groups.
key_points: North Korean state‑backed hackers stole at least $6.3 billion from Binance in a 20‑minute breach that began with a compromised engineer’s laptop.
Binance has frozen about half the stolen crypto and is collaborating with law‑enforcement and blockchain firms to recover assets while suspending deposits and withdrawals.
Security researchers confirmed the attackers, known as TraderTraitor, did not access Binance’s private keys but used a service container to submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.

posts.title: Mistral releases weights for its trillion-parameter AI model, targeting cybersecurity | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lucas Ropek
posts.summary: Mistral has released the weights for its trillion‑parameter open‑source model, Mistral Large 4 (ML4), enabling businesses and governments to download and run the system on‑prem. The model, dubbed "Le Chonk," claims state‑of‑the‑art performance in cybersecurity tasks while using 47% fewer tokens per task than the Chinese competitor GLM‑5.3, making it more economical. By providing open weights, Mistral argues that organizations can own and control advanced AI defense tools without relying on closed‑model providers. The release underscores a broader shift toward open‑weight AI as a means of empowering sovereign cyber defense capabilities.
key_points: Mistral has made the weights for its trillion‑parameter model ML4 publicly available on Hugging Face and via API.
ML4 outperforms the open‑weight competitor GLM‑5.3 in cybersecurity tasks while using 47% fewer tokens, reducing compute costs.
Open‑weight release allows enterprises and governments to deploy the model on‑prem, ensuring data sovereignty and continuous access.
Mistral positions the model as a tool for empowerment, emphasizing open‑source benefits over closed‑model dominance.

posts.title: AI law firm Crosby bids on disintegrating, famed firm Weil Gotshal | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: Crosby, a two‑year‑old AI‑first law firm, has made a bid to acquire key assets of the dissolving Wall Street boutique Weil, Gotshal & Manges, including its trademark, brand and internal data, while also courting some of its 1,200 lawyers. The prestigious firm is winding down after its heir apparent declined the leadership role, top lawyers departed, and a planned merger with Willkie Farr & Gallagher fell through. Crosby’s founders argue that their AI‑powered platform can deliver legal services at unprecedented speed, positioning the startup as a potential successor to Weil’s legacy. With roughly $85 million raised—including a $60 million Series B led by Lux and Index—Crosby’s move could signal a broader shift toward AI‑driven legal practices.
key_points: Crosby is bidding to acquire Weil Gotshal’s assets and lawyers
Weil Gotshal is dissolving after leadership and merger setbacks
Crosby’s AI‑powered model aims to transform legal service delivery
Crosby has raised $85 million, including a $60 million Series B

posts.title: DoorDash said it's only received 'several hundred' orders from AI agents | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: DoorDash disclosed during its third‑quarter earnings call that it has only received several hundred orders from third‑party AI agents such as Muse, Instinct, and Fo, a tiny fraction of its average 3 million daily deliveries. CEO Tony Xu described the agent‑ordering space as still dynamic but not yet dominant, noting that most customers continue to order through the DoorDash app. The company is also developing its own agents—including a text‑to‑order bot, a CLI agent, and a chatbot called Ask DoorDash—to better understand and potentially partner with external agent makers. DoorDash sees future opportunities for advertising within these agents as the broader agent‑based ordering ecosystem evolves.
key_points: DoorDash has only received several hundred AI‑agent orders in Q3, compared to 3 million daily deliveries
CEO Tony Xu says agent ordering is a dynamic but minor part of the business
DoorDash is building its own agents and exploring partnerships and advertising with third‑party agents
The agent‑based ordering market is still developing, with mixed adoption by retailers like Amazon and Walmart

posts.title: Binance pauses withdrawals as hackers suspected of stealing billions in crypto | TechCrunch
posts.author: Zack Whittaker
posts.summary: Binance has temporarily suspended withdrawals on multiple networks after a suspected security breach that may have drained up to $5.7 billion from its hot wallets, according to the exchange’s statement. Founder Changpeng Zhao confirmed the hack on X and said user funds would be fully covered, while Circle and Tether froze $800 million and $1.56 billion respectively to protect assets. The incident, which could rank among the largest crypto thefts in history, follows Bybit’s record $1.4 billion breach in 2025. Binance’s security team is actively investigating the incident and urges users to remain cautious of scams.
key_points: Binance suspended withdrawals after a suspected hack that may have drained up to $5.7 billion from hot wallets
Circle and Tether froze $800 million and $1.56 billion respectively to protect user funds
Founder Changpeng Zhao confirmed the hack and said user funds would be fully covered
The breach could rank among the largest crypto thefts, following Bybit’s $1.4 billion incident in 2025

posts.title: Make game-changing connections at Founder Summit with Braindate | TechCrunch
posts.author: TechCrunch Events
posts.summary: TechCrunch’s Founder Summit 2026, scheduled for November 4 at Boston’s SoWa Power Station, will use Braindate’s platform to help founders, investors, and operators schedule one‑on‑one and small‑group conversations around specific topics such as scaling, fundraising, and product‑market fit. The event offers a buy‑one‑get‑one‑free ticket promotion, allowing attendees to bring a guest at no extra cost. Sessions will feature industry leaders like Kent Bennett, Dave Balter, and Toast co‑founder Steve Fredette, while breakout roundtables and live pitch tests provide additional networking and learning opportunities. The summit’s smaller, hands‑on format aims to turn accidental networking into intentional, question‑driven dialogue that can extend beyond the day’s agenda.
key_points: Founder Summit 2026 uses Braindate to enable targeted networking on topics like scaling and fundraising
Attendees can purchase one pass and receive a free second pass for a guest
The event features talks from Bessemer, True Ventures, and Toast, plus interactive roundtables and live pitch sessions
It is held at SoWa Power Station in Boston on November 4

posts.title: Can AI data centers be mass-produced like cars? This startup aims to find out | TechCrunch
posts.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
posts.summary: Runware, an AI infrastructure startup, plans to mass‑produce its Sonic Inference Pods by building a factory that assembles modular data centers on a production line, aiming for 30 MW of capacity per day by 2028. The company’s Romanian plant will ramp up from a few weeks per pod to a one‑day build, with pods online within 48 hours of delivery. Runware claims its closed‑loop cooling and use of standard components keep costs low, while it has already secured $1 B in committed interest for over 20 MW of pods. If successful, the factory could deliver roughly as much capacity in a year as the U.S. was expected to add this year, positioning modular AI data centers as the future standard for rapid deployment.
key_points: Runware aims to produce 30 MW of data‑center capacity per day by 2028, equivalent to nearly 1 GW per month.
The company’s factory will reduce pod build time from three weeks to one day and bring pods online within 48 hours.
Runware has secured $1 B in committed interest for its Sonic pods and plans to expand to the U.S. and other regions.
The pods use closed‑loop liquid cooling, are silent, and rely on renewable energy where possible.

posts.title: AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says — but first, it will spend big | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lucas Ropek
posts.summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy reiterated that AWS could become a trillion‑dollar revenue business, but to reach that goal the company will need to raise capital expenditures to $220 billion in 2026 and more in 2027 to build AI‑driven infrastructure. AWS revenue grew 39% in the latest quarter and is projected to grow 40% in 2027 and 2028, with a current run‑rate of $184 billion. Jassy framed the heavy spending as a once‑in‑a‑lifetime investment to capture the surge in enterprise AI demand, though investors remained wary and shares fell about 6% after the call. The announcement underscores the broader trend of cloud providers investing heavily in AI while chasing record growth.
key_points: AWS aims for $1 trillion annual revenue within 5–10 years, backed by a projected 40% growth in 2027 and 2028.
Amazon plans $220 billion in 2026 capital expenditures, mainly for AWS, with further spending in 2027.
AWS revenue rose 39% YoY in the last quarter, reaching a $184 billion run‑rate.
Investors expressed concern over the high AI infrastructure spend, causing a 6% drop in Amazon shares post‑call.

posts.title: Elon Musk is 'truly a genius,' says Vladimir Putin | TechCrunch
posts.author: Amanda Silberling
posts.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin praised Elon Musk as a genius during the Russia‑Africa Summit, noting that the two leaders are in close contact regarding Russia’s Rassvet satellite project, which aims to rival SpaceX’s Starlink. Putin highlighted that Musk’s network already hosts over 5,000 satellites while Russia is only beginning its efforts. The article also discusses recent tensions over Starlink’s military use in Ukraine, where Musk reportedly limited access after Ukrainian forces used the service for offensive drone strikes, a move that raised concerns about the impact on Ukraine’s defense. The piece underscores how the evolving relationship between Musk and Putin could have significant geopolitical and military implications amid the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.
key_points: Putin lauds Musk as a genius and says they are in close contact about Russia’s Rassvet satellite project.
Musk’s Starlink network already has more than 5,000 satellites, far ahead of Russia’s nascent program.
Musk limited Ukraine’s Starlink access after the country used the service for offensive drone strikes, sparking fears of a collapse in Ukrainian defense capabilities.
The potential partnership between Musk and Putin could influence military technology access and geopolitical dynamics in the region.

posts.title: Waymo taps Toyota to supply robotaxis for Japan and the UK | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kirsten Korosec
posts.summary: Waymo has announced a partnership with Toyota to supply autonomous bZ4X electric vehicles for robotaxi operations in Japan and the UK. Toyota will build the 2027 bZ4X models at its Takaoka plant and integrate Waymo’s self‑driving system, with initial testing slated for Japan next year and plans to roll out the service in other right‑hand‑drive markets such as London. The deal follows an 18‑month exploratory agreement and positions Waymo to expand its robotaxi fleet while opening the door to future collaboration on personal Toyota vehicles and road‑safety initiatives.
key_points: Waymo will test autonomous Toyota bZ4X vehicles in Japan next year
Toyota will manufacture 2027 bZ4X models with Waymo’s system at its Takaoka factory
The partnership aims to expand robotaxi services to the UK and other right‑hand‑drive markets
Future collaboration could bring Waymo technology into personal Toyota vehicles and improve road safety

posts.title: You don't need to believe in a god to get a religious exemption from using AI at work | TechCrunch
posts.author: Amanda Silberling
posts.summary: David Durman, a nontheistic humanist and University of Kentucky administrator, became the first humanist to secure a religious exemption from using artificial intelligence at work, citing concerns that AI undermines critical thinking and human well‑being. The American Humanist Association helped him obtain legal protection, and the university approved the accommodation while allowing him to continue performing his essential duties. Durman’s case follows a similar exemption granted to Unitarian Universalist engineer Erin Maus and signals that secular workers can now pursue comparable protections. The move highlights growing anxiety over AI’s impact on human dignity and the need for workplace policies that respect diverse philosophical convictions.
key_points: David Durman, a humanist, secured a religious exemption from AI use at work.
The American Humanist Association facilitated the legal protection and the university approved the accommodation.
Durman’s case follows a similar exemption granted to Unitarian Universalist engineer Erin Maus.
The precedent allows secular workers to seek comparable workplace accommodations.

posts.title: AI execs may be too out of touch to build for the general public | TechCrunch
posts.author: Amanda Silberling
posts.summary: Marissa Mayer’s new AI assistant Dazzle drew criticism for suggesting it could describe her daughter and help plan her birthday, prompting accusations that Silicon Valley leaders are out of touch with everyday people. The backlash echoes similar reactions to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s remarks about using ChatGPT to raise children and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s vision of AI‑driven social connections. A Pew Research Center study shows that half of U.S. adults fear AI will erode meaningful relationships, while only a small minority believe it will help. The article argues that tech executives’ focus on efficiency and automation risks turning human relationships into commodified products, leaving society to outsource emotional needs to machines.
key_points: Marissa Mayer’s Dazzle sparked backlash for its child‑related use cases, highlighting a disconnect between AI leaders and the public.
OpenAI and Meta CEOs have made public statements that AI could replace or augment parenting and social interactions, fueling public concern.
A Pew study finds 50% of U.S. adults worry AI will reduce meaningful relationships, with only 5% seeing benefits.
The piece warns that prioritizing efficiency over human connection may commodify relationships and deepen societal isolation.

posts.title: Google’s Genie 4 world model adds audio, more realistic worlds, and real-time steering | TechCrunch
posts.author: Rebecca Bellan
posts.summary: Google DeepMind unveiled its latest world model, Genie 4, in a research preview, offering photorealistic interactive environments that can be edited on the fly and generate matching real‑time audio, including music, ambient sounds, and dialogue. The model doubles the scene‑duration of its predecessor, supports free‑form changes such as weather or camera angle, and is tightly coupled with Gemini, which plans steps and checks frames while Genie renders the visuals. Potential applications span gaming, interactive learning, robotics, and even film prototyping, though the team notes gaps in detail consistency and audio accuracy. Genie 4 is currently available to trusted testers, with broader rollout planned for Google AI Ultra subscribers and Gemini API partners.
key_points: Genie 4 adds photorealistic worlds, real‑time audio, and free‑form edits to its predecessor
It is integrated with Gemini, enabling step planning and real‑time simulation
Use cases include gaming, interactive learning, robotics, and film prototyping
The model still has gaps in detail drift and audio accuracy

posts.title: GM reaches $220M settlement over selling drivers' private data | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kirsten Korosec
posts.summary: General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to 36 states to settle allegations that it illegally sold drivers’ private location and behavior data to data brokers, a practice that was exposed by a New York Times investigation. The settlement requires GM to obtain express consent before collecting or sharing driving data and to have a third‑party audit its privacy program, aligning with prior agreements with California and the FTC. Although GM discontinued its Smart Driver program in 2024, the company remains under scrutiny for how it handles connected‑vehicle data and has pledged to stop selling personally identifiable information while still allowing anonymized data sharing with partners. The deal underscores the growing regulatory focus on privacy as automakers increasingly rely on sensor‑rich, software‑centric vehicles and new AI‑powered services like OnStar’s personal assistant.
key_points: GM will pay $220 million to settle claims that it sold private driving data to data brokers.
The settlement mandates express consent for data collection and a third‑party audit of GM’s privacy program.
GM discontinued its Smart Driver program but remains bound by FTC and state orders that restrict data sharing.
GM is positioning its new AI assistant and future connected‑vehicle features around enhanced privacy controls and transparency.

posts.title: The R2 SUV is already Rivian's best-selling vehicle | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sean O'Kane
posts.summary: Rivian’s new R2 SUV has become the company’s best‑selling vehicle in Q3, prompting the automaker to lift its annual delivery guidance to a floor of 67,000 units. The company built 19,751 vehicles and delivered 19,248 in the quarter, a 45% year‑over‑year jump that helped it generate $2.2 billion in revenue while posting a $913 million net loss. The R2, priced just under $60,000, is driving demand in a market that has lost the $7,500 federal EV tax credit, and Rivian plans to introduce lower‑priced trims later this year. This surge in sales marks a turning point for Rivian, which has struggled to ship more than 50,000 vehicles annually for three years.
key_points: R2 SUV became Rivian’s best‑selling vehicle in Q3
Rivian raised its annual delivery guidance to 67,000 units
Q3 production and deliveries rose 45% year‑over‑year
R2 is priced under $60,000 and will see lower‑priced trims later this year

posts.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings acquires ADT | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: Thrive Holdings, a spin‑out of Thrive Capital and backed by OpenAI, has agreed to acquire ADT for $10 per share, valuing the deal at about $7.6 billion in equity and $15.3 billion enterprise value. The acquisition positions Thrive to build a smart‑home security platform, leveraging its AI expertise and OpenAI’s models to develop new physical‑security products. ADT already works with Apple and Google, and the partnership is expected to accelerate the rollout of AI‑powered cameras and other home‑security devices. The deal underscores the growing convergence of AI and physical security as major tech players expand into the smart‑home market.
key_points: Thrive Holdings acquires ADT for $10 per share ($7.6B equity, $15.3B enterprise value).
OpenAI will supply AI models and engineers to help build new security products for Thrive’s portfolio.
The move signals a broader trend of AI integration in physical security and smart‑home ecosystems.

posts.title: Meta quietly launches an AI fashion app called Style Sketch | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aisha Malik
posts.summary: Meta quietly launched Style Sketch, an AI fashion app that builds a virtual closet from Instagram photos or manually uploaded images and suggests outfit combinations tailored to a user’s style. The app offers realistic virtual try‑ons matched to body shape and skin tone, and can generate day‑by‑day outfit plans for trips based on weather and itinerary. It is currently available on iOS and Android in Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. The release is part of Meta’s broader strategy to ship more AI‑driven apps, following recent launches like Waddle World, Pocket, and Vibes.
key_points: Meta launched Style Sketch, an AI fashion app that creates a virtual closet from Instagram photos or manual uploads.
The app suggests outfits, offers realistic try‑ons, and can plan trip outfits using weather and itinerary data.
It is available on iOS and Android in Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand.
Style Sketch is part of Meta’s push to release a larger number of AI‑powered apps.

posts.title: Granola crunches up a dictation feature to compete with Wispr | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: Granola, the meeting‑notetaking startup, has launched an unlimited‑word dictation feature that works across all Mac applications by pressing the Fn key, and it will soon be available on iOS and Windows. The new tool cleans and formats spoken language into text, allowing users to dictate notes, prompts, emails, and messages without limits on any plan. This move positions Granola to compete directly with Wispr, which recently added a meeting‑notetaker to its dictation suite, as both companies are valued at roughly $1.5 billion and $2 billion respectively. The launch reflects a broader trend of voice‑AI startups converging from single‑purpose apps into multi‑feature platforms that capture and process speech for productivity.
key_points: Granola adds unlimited‑word dictation to its meeting‑notetaking suite on Mac.
Feature is available to all plans with no usage limits.
Granola and Wispr are valued at $1.5 billion and $2 billion, respectively.
Voice‑AI apps are moving beyond single‑purpose tools toward comprehensive speech‑capture solutions.

posts.title: Wabi, the AI agent that builds mini apps, now valued at $1.25B after latest round | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Wabi, the AI personal agent founded by former Replika CEO Eugenia Kuyda, closed a $55 million funding round that values the company at $1.25 billion after pivoting from a prompt‑based app builder to a messenger‑style AI that can create mini‑apps for everyday tasks. The round was led by IVP with participation from Andreessen Horowitz, Forerunner, Amazon Alexa Fund, and high‑profile angels including Tobi Lütke, Marc Benioff, Marissa Mayer, Dick Costolo, and Alex Pall. Investors see Wabi’s agentic approach as a timely bet in a market that has seen other AI agents, such as Instinct, raise $1 billion at a $10 billion valuation. The move underscores the growing interest in AI tools that move beyond text boxes to act as personal assistants capable of building functional interfaces on demand.
key_points: Wabi raised $55 million, valuing it at $1.25 billion after pivoting to an AI messenger that builds mini‑apps
The round was led by IVP and included Andreessen Horowitz, Amazon Alexa Fund, and notable angels like Tobi Lütke and Marc Benioff
Investors view Wabi’s agentic model as a strong bet amid a surge of AI‑assistant startups such as Instinct
Founder Eugenia Kuyda brings experience from Replika, positioning Wabi to expand beyond simple prompt‑based apps

posts.title: Amazon reported booming cloud revenue but otherwise missed expectations | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: Amazon reported its third‑quarter earnings on Thursday, missing analysts’ expectations for total revenue and earnings per share. The cloud unit, Amazon Web Services, was the bright spot, posting a 39% year‑over‑year revenue growth and beating revenue forecasts. However, free cash flow for the trailing 12 months fell to a negative $42.4 billion, a sharp reversal from the $14.8 billion positive free cash flow reported for the same period ended September 30 2025, largely due to heavy spending on AI. Amazon reiterated a 2026 capital‑expenditure outlook of about $220 billion, roughly matching the $240‑$247 billion net‑sales forecast for the fourth quarter, underscoring the company’s aggressive investment in artificial intelligence.
key_points: Amazon missed Q3 revenue and EPS expectations.
AWS grew 39% YoY and beat revenue forecasts.
Free cash flow turned negative $42.4B, driven by AI spending.
Amazon plans $220B capex for 2026, close to Q4 sales forecast.

posts.title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it's shifting to a logged-in experience | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Reddit announced it will shift to a primarily logged‑in experience as search traffic dries up amid the rise of AI‑powered search. The move is intended to protect data from AI scraping and enable lucrative licensing deals with model providers while helping the company monetize a shrinking user base. Despite a 2% year‑over‑year decline in U.S. daily active users, Reddit’s revenue jumped 53% YoY to $895 million, driven by a 54% rise in advertising and a 35% increase in non‑advertising AI data licensing. The transition will be tested in select markets outside the U.S. in Q4, with no firm global rollout date yet announced.
key_points: Reddit is moving to a logged‑in model to safeguard data and pursue AI licensing amid falling search referrals
Search traffic referrals dropped over 1 million per week in October, contributing to a 2% YoY decline in U.S. daily active users
Revenue grew 53% YoY to $895 million, with advertising up 54% to $847 million and non‑advertising AI data licensing up 35% to $48 million
Logged‑in users offer higher ad value and personalization, and the change will be rolled out gradually starting in Q4

posts.title: Rivian expands joint venture with VW to include AI assistant | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kirsten Korosec
posts.summary: Rivian and Volkswagen Group have expanded their $5.8 billion joint venture to license Rivian’s AI voice‑assistant technology to VW. The assistant, which debuted in Rivian’s R1S SUV and R1T pickup in May 2026 and R2 SUV in October, could first appear in VW’s low‑cost ID EVERY1 hatchback. The move underscores Rivian’s push for vertical integration, allowing it to bundle its electrical architecture, software, and compute platform across partners. VW’s increased investment and the partnership aim to give the German automaker a modern, software‑centric platform that rivals Tesla’s offerings.
key_points: $5.8B joint venture now includes AI assistant licensing
First VW vehicle to use Rivian tech will be ID EVERY1
Rivian’s AI assistant launched in 2026 and supports future third‑party agents
The partnership highlights Rivian’s vertical integration strategy

posts.title: SuperMe raises $20M for its network of AI expert profiles | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: SuperMe, a 2024 startup that builds AI personas from real experts and matches user questions to a curated group chat, has raised $20 million in funding led by Forerunner’s Kirsten Green with participation from Greylock Partners. The platform aggregates knowledge from public sources and connected apps to create AI profiles of industry leaders such as VCs and entrepreneurs, allowing users to ask questions and receive expert‑style answers. While the service remains free for now, SuperMe plans to introduce a paid tier after a limited number of free queries and is hiring to enhance its AI matching algorithms and expand its expert network. The funding underscores the growing interest in hybrid human‑AI knowledge platforms and positions SuperMe to scale its network on both sides of the market.
key_points: SuperMe secured $20M in funding led by Forerunner’s Kirsten Green with Greylock participation
The platform creates AI personas of real experts and matches user queries to a group chat of those personas
The startup plans to monetize after a free tier and is hiring to improve AI matching and expand expert coverage

posts.title: Amazon updates Alexa to help you manage shopping lists and subscriptions and update delivery instructions | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: Amazon has expanded Alexa’s shopping capabilities with over 100 new features that let users create and manage lists, adjust subscription schedules, and edit delivery instructions. The update also lets Alexa answer questions about Prime and Audible memberships, billing, and payment issues. These enhancements come ahead of the holiday season and build on Amazon’s earlier AI‑centric shopping tools such as the shopping assistant and product‑notification service. According to Amazon, agentic features have grown eightfold since the start of the year and more than 400 million consumers have used Alexa for shopping in the past year.
key_points: Alexa now supports over 100 new shopping features, including list management and subscription adjustments.
Users can edit delivery instructions and change addresses directly through voice commands.
The assistant can answer questions about Prime, Audible, billing, and payment issues.
Amazon reports an eight‑fold increase in agentic feature usage and 400 million shoppers using Alexa for purchases.

posts.title: Fan-fiction site Archive of Our Own (AO3) could be offline for up to 4 weeks after security incident | TechCrunch
posts.author: Amanda Silberling
posts.summary: Archive of Our Own (AO3), the fan‑fiction platform run by the nonprofit Organization for Transformative Works, announced that a security incident has forced the site offline and could keep it down for up to four weeks. The incident was discovered during routine maintenance, and while the scope is still being investigated, the team has not ruled out the possibility that user account data—including usernames, emails, IPs, and hashed passwords—may have been accessed. AO3, which is built on Ruby on Rails rather than PHP, is not linked to the recent PHP vulnerabilities, and the organization has urged users to change passwords on other sites as a precaution. The outage has already sparked widespread concern, with the status page receiving millions of views and the community scrambling for updates.
key_points: AO3 offline due to a security incident, with downtime expected up to four weeks
User account data may have been accessed; password changes are advised
The site runs on Ruby on Rails, unrelated to recent PHP vulnerabilities

posts.title: Deepgram acquires Pipecat-maker Daily to bolster its voice AI infrastructure | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: Deepgram has announced the acquisition of Daily, the creators of the open‑source Pipecat framework, without disclosing a price but pledging to keep Pipecat open source. Pipecat orchestrates voice and video streams, integrating speech‑to‑text, large language models, and text‑to‑speech while reducing latency, giving Deepgram a deeper real‑time communication stack. The deal positions Deepgram to expand beyond voice into broader real‑time AI‑native software and to launch the Real‑Time Context Standard, an open protocol for voice agents. Both companies, alumni of Y Combinator’s 2016 batch, emphasize an engineering culture that supports open‑source collaboration and vendor‑neutral ecosystems.
key_points: Deepgram acquires Daily and commits to keeping Pipecat open source
Pipecat is a real‑time orchestration framework for voice, video, STT, LLM, and TTS
The acquisition broadens Deepgram’s real‑time communication capabilities beyond voice
Both firms share a Y Combinator 2016 heritage and a focus on open‑source collaboration

posts.title: Ex-Palantir execs launch Dream with $17M from a16z to build AI world models for construction | TechCrunch
posts.author: Marina Temkin
posts.summary: Ex‑Palantir executives Andy Elder and Arjun Mathur have launched Dream, a startup that uses AI‑powered world models to automate building design and engineering. The company raised $17 million in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, with additional backing from SV Angel, XYZ and Zigg Capital. Dream’s “structural cognition” model is trained on over 100 million square feet of U.S. building data and produces structurally sound designs that can replace legacy AEC tools like AutoCAD and Revit. The platform is already deployed on 10 projects in Texas and California and aims to boost productivity in the construction sector, which has seen fewer new buildings and rising costs.
key_points: Dream, founded by former Palantir execs, uses AI world models to generate structurally sound building designs.
The startup secured $17 million in seed funding from Andreessen Horowitz, SV Angel, XYZ and Zigg Capital.
Its “structural cognition” model is trained on more than 100 million square feet of U.S. building data.
Dream is already used on 10 active projects in Texas and California, targeting replacement of legacy AEC software.

posts.title: Agent identity startup Mintive lands Cowboy Ventures, Coatue, angels Jeff Dean, Andrej Karpathy | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: Mintive, an agent‑identity startup founded by former Coursera engineer Jiquan Ngiam and Google Brain TensorFlow co‑creator Vijay Vasudevan, has raised a total of $11 million, including a $7 million seed round led by Cowboy Ventures and backing from Coatue, Operator Collective, Hustle Fund and angels such as Jeff Dean and Andrej Karpathy. The company offers an end‑to‑end platform that manages agent identities, authorizations, cost routing and monitoring, with a focus on rapid, button‑click deployment that has already attracted 50 enterprise customers including Coursera, Stability AI and the University of Michigan. Mintive enters a crowded field of agent‑management solutions from Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and numerous startups, but its founders’ deep enterprise AI experience and emphasis on ease of use set it apart. The funding and early customer traction signal growing investor confidence in infrastructure that governs and provisions AI agents for businesses.
key_points: Mintive secured $11 million in total funding, led by Cowboy Ventures, with high‑profile angels Jeff Dean and Andrej Karpathy
Founders bring deep AI enterprise experience from Coursera, Google Brain, and TensorFlow
The platform offers end‑to‑end agent identity, access control, cost routing, and monitoring with quick, button‑click deployment
Already 50 enterprise customers, including Coursera, Stability AI, and the University of Michigan

posts.title: Microsoft hits 10 quarters of record-breaking revenue in a row | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: Microsoft reported a record quarterly revenue of $92.3 billion, a 19% year‑over‑year increase, marking the company’s tenth consecutive quarter of record‑breaking sales. Net income rose to $36.6 billion, up 32% on a GAAP basis, driven largely by the $63.9 billion in cloud revenue, which grew 30% YoY. The cloud segment included $33.2 billion from Azure, $28 billion from Microsoft 365, and $10 billion from OpenAI services, while capital expenditures topped $45.2 billion, another all‑time quarterly record. Microsoft also announced that its commercial remaining performance obligation—future revenue commitments—jumped 73% to $677 billion.
key_points: Microsoft achieved its tenth straight quarter of record revenue, reaching $92.3 billion
Cloud revenue hit $63.9 billion, with Azure contributing $33.2 billion and OpenAI $10 billion
Capital expenditures set a new quarterly record at $45.2 billion

posts.title: Anthropic just launched tools to show companies what their AI spending is buying | TechCrunch
posts.author: Tim Fernholz
posts.summary: Anthropic has unveiled a new suite of reporting tools that let enterprise customers track token spend, cost, and workflow performance, aiming to demonstrate ROI and lock in users. The launch follows the company’s Q2 operating profit and a 900% net revenue retention, underscoring strong enterprise adoption. The reports provide granular data on team output, cost, and bottlenecks, plus recommendations for improvement, while explicitly stating that the data will not be used for model training. This move comes amid growing CFO concern over unplanned AI spend, with a Jellyfish survey showing Anthropic’s Claude Code accounts for nearly a third of code changes and has seen ten‑fold spend growth, now about 2% of engineering budgets.
key_points: Anthropic released reporting tools to give enterprise users a detailed view of token spend and ROI.
The suite offers cost breakdowns, workflow analysis, and improvement suggestions without training models on the data.
Anthropic’s Q2 operating profit and 900% net revenue retention highlight strong enterprise traction.
A Jellyfish survey shows Anthropic tools drive 10x spend growth and account for ~1/3 of code changes, costing ~2% of engineering budgets.

posts.title: Bluesky blocks links to leaked DHS employee data as government seeks takedowns | TechCrunch
posts.author: Zack Whittaker
posts.summary: Bluesky has begun blocking links to the nonprofit DDoSecrets site that hosts a leaked dataset of more than 40,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employee records, after the agency disclosed a breach of its login system. The stolen data included names, work phone numbers and email addresses of employees from agencies such as Customs and Border Protection and Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and was made publicly available by DDoSecrets. Bluesky’s chief operating officer explained that the block was chosen to protect privacy while still allowing discussion of the data, and the company plans to update its block message wording. Homeland Security has also filed takedown notices through security vendor ZeroFox, which has authority to act on the department’s behalf until 2028, and the domain registrar CentralNic has taken the site offline for now.
key_points: Bluesky blocked links to DDoSecrets after a DHS data breach exposed 40,000 employee records
The leaked data included professional contact information that was shared without consent
Homeland Security used ZeroFox to file takedown notices and the domain registrar has taken the site offline
Bluesky chose to block links rather than remove individual posts to preserve public discussion

posts.title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart for $17B | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aisha Malik
posts.summary: DoorDash announced it will acquire Instacart for $17 billion, paying $65 per share. The deal merges DoorDash’s restaurant‑takeout dominance with Instacart’s grocery‑delivery network, keeping Instacart’s brand and technology separate until closing. Both CEOs highlighted that the combination will give retailers and shoppers better tools and lower‑cost delivery, while the transaction is expected to close in late 2027 or early 2028. posts.title: Meta has a new AI pet app called Waddle World | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: Meta launched Waddle World, an AI‑powered virtual pet app similar to Tamagotchi, available in the Philippines on iOS and Android. The release follows Meta’s other AI experiments like Pocket and Vibes, and may signal a cautious approach to companion AI amid legal concerns.

posts.title: Google expands AI Search ads globally as core ad growth slows | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lauren Forristal
posts.summary: Google announced it is expanding AI-powered Search ads to international markets as a response to slowing growth in its core search advertising business. posts.title: Microsoft recorded $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI | TechCrunch
posts.author: Rebecca Bellan
posts.summary: Microsoft reported $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, representing nearly 11% of its $92.3 billion quarterly revenue. posts.title: Wiz’s CTO on PHP2Shell and the coming 'vulnpocalypse' | TechCrunch
posts.author: Theresa Loconsolo
posts.summary: Last week, two critical bugs were discovered in PHP, the language that powers about 70% of websites, forcing many organizations to take sites offline while patches were developed. Tomer Schwartz, CTO of Exposure Management & AppSec at Wiz, joined a rapid‑response effort alongside OpenAI, the research group Calif, and the PHP core team to fix the vulnerabilities and discuss the broader implications of AI‑accelerated vulnerability discovery. In a TechCrunch Equity podcast interview, Schwartz explained how the scramble unfolded, why manual patching is unsustainable, and how early‑stage startups can build security into their products from the outset. He also warned that the PHP incident is just the beginning of a “vulnpocalypse” that will grow as AI tools make finding and exploiting new flaws faster.

posts.title: US investigated Chinese spy plot aimed at Nvidia CEO | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: U.S. intelligence agencies have been surveilling Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore‑based Megaspeed, for about a year after she was photographed alongside Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at business dinners. Sources say Huang’s close proximity to Jensen could have allowed her to gather information on Nvidia’s plans to ship advanced chips to China, raising concerns that she might have been acting as a Chinese spy. Nvidia has denied the allegation, stating that meetings with customers are routine and that no sensitive trade secrets were shared. The investigation follows Megaspeed’s own probe by the Commerce Department for allegedly helping Chinese firms sidestep AI‑chip export restrictions.

posts.title: Upwind raises $400M after walking away from Datadog acquisition offer | TechCrunch
posts.author: Marina Temkin
posts.summary: Upwind, a San Francisco AI‑driven cloud security startup, closed a $400 million Series C round at a $3.8 billion valuation led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Greylock and Craft Ventures. posts.title: Hacker stole personnel data about thousands of Homeland Security employees, including CBP and ICE agents | TechCrunch
posts.author: Zack Whittaker
posts.summary: A hacker known as Department of Peace stole more than 40,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employee records from an Okta single sign‑on system, exposing names, job titles, emails, phone numbers and office locations. The breach, dated to mid‑August, includes 21,000 Customs and Border Protection staff, 10,000 Immigration and Customs Enforcement employees, about 1,000 Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency workers, and other agency personnel, representing roughly one‑fifth of DHS’s workforce. The data was released to journalist maia arson crimew and then to DDoSecrets, revealing not only personal information but also access to surveillance tools such as Penlink, Headspace, and Mobile Fortify, raising concerns about tech vendors. DHS has acknowledged the incident and is investigating, while Okta denies any compromise, and the breach adds to a series of recent government data losses.

posts.title: Trump DOE loans $5B to nuclear plants that will power data centers | TechCrunch
posts.author: Tim De Chant

Most of the new output is already earmarked for hyperscalers, with Google, Meta and Amazon each purchasing power from several of the Illinois sites, plus Maryland and Pennsylvania plants. Constellation plans to spend over $7 billion to add 1,080 MW of nuclear capacity for these tech giants, and the loans could lower financing costs for the upgrades. posts.title: TikTok expands into restaurant guides with 'Must Eat' feature | TechCrunch

posts.title: Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro pushes laptop pricing to a new extreme | TechCrunch

posts.title: Microsoft just shared Azure's actual revenue in dollars: $33.2 billion | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aditya Mehta

posts.title: As AI agents reshape the web, Google opens Gemini and Search to more apps | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Google has launched a Connected Apps Platform that lets developers link their services to the company’s AI experiences in Gemini and Search, enabling users to perform actions like designing a flyer with Canva or building a playlist with YouTube Music directly from the AI interface. posts.title: Free Fire returns to India as Garena launches localized version four years after ban | TechCrunch
posts.author: Jagmeet Singh

posts.title: South Korea's financial industry hit by fresh wave of cyberattacks | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kate Park
posts.summary: South Korea’s financial sector has faced a new wave of cyberattacks, targeting brokerages Daishin Securities and Mirae Asset Global Investments as well as the crypto exchange Bithumb. The breaches, which followed a September assault linked to a China‑based hacker using the AI penetration‑testing tool Artex, exposed personal data of 38,490 Daishin customers and raised concerns that other firms may have suffered similar compromises. In response, the Financial Services Commission has urged tighter cybersecurity safeguards and announced plans to audit dozens of private‑sector IT systems, while the affected firms have begun notifying customers and cooperating with authorities. The incidents echo a broader regional trend, with Japan’s GMO Internet also reporting a cyber incident, underscoring the growing threat of AI‑driven hacking across Asia.

Attacks linked to a China‑based hacker using the AI tool Artex, following a September wave
South Korean regulator demands stronger cybersecurity and will audit private‑sector IT systems

posts.title: Reddit is the latest platform to embrace the 'For You' feed | TechCrunch

The algorithm‑curated feed blends posts from a user’s subscribed communities with personalized suggestions to help them discover new topics and conversations. Reddit says the change is meant to boost connection, participation, and belonging, and users can toggle between feeds at any time. The rollout will be global over the next few weeks, though some early testers have voiced frustration with the shift away from a purely community‑focused view.

posts.title: Voice AI in vogue: Nvidia releases new open transcription model | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort

posts.title: Kodiak lands first commercial deal to supply driverless trucks for public highways | TechCrunch

posts.title: Jio shares surge 21% in market debut after blockbuster India IPO | TechCrunch

posts.title: The data center boom has an upside: innovation for the US grid | TechCrunch

posts.title: Japan internet giant GMO says hackers posted stolen customer data | TechCrunch
